kind: teacher-forced PROXY: human-written text stands in for K3's greedy output and a byte-level BPE trained here stands in for K3's tokenizer; a draft is accepted when it equals the next ids of the text. Not a measurement of K3 and not a tokens-per-second figure.

tokenizer.kind: proxy byte-level BPE (tokenizers 0.23.2); K3's own tokenizer ships with the checkpoint and was not available
tokenizer.disjointness: no evaluation document or any copy of it is in the training text: evaluation sources are this repository, the Python standard library and the evaluation half of package markdown (split by package); training files sharing more than 25% of their lines of 24+ characters with any evaluation text were dropped
tokenizer.framing: every turn is [user] prompt [end] [assistant] answer [end], the three markers being ids outside the BPE vocabulary; the answer's [end] is part of the output the drafts are checked against

cost_model.verify_step: S(n) = a_T + a_E*u(n) + a_C*n + eps, n = drafted + 1
cost_model.today: a partial acceptance (m < nd) adds a_T + a_E*u(m+1) + a_C*(m+1)
cost_model.emitted_per_step: m + 1, truncated at the end of the turn
cost_model.speedup: emitted ids / summed step cost, pooled over the documents
cost_model.eps_sensitivity: with a per-verify overhead eps, cost rises by eps * fired steps: speedup_eps = emitted / (cost + eps * fired), computable from these rows

method.draft_points: every step the engine would take when its greedy output equals the text: from each point it jumps by what that step emits. The first id of each answer comes from prefill, where the engine never drafts, and is excluded.
method.split: 20% of each corpus's documents (hash of the document id) are calibration: they fit P3's table and choose P2's defaults; every reported row is on the other 80%
method.bootstrap: 2000 resamples of evaluation documents with replacement; 95% percentile intervals; the same resamples for every policy, so differences are paired
method.per_position_acceptance: pos_i = P(draft i accepted | drafted and 1..i-1 accepted)

policies.P0: spec_draft() as in src/cli/k3_run.c (port verified against crafted and random sequences); N = --spec cap
policies.P1: most recent occurrence of the suffix 4-gram, else 3-gram, else 2-gram; copy its continuation up to the end of the history; no gate
policies.P2: longest suffix match (suffix automaton), most recent occurrence, fires when match length >= min_len, drafts N ids, periodic copy past the end of the history; the no-overlap variant stops at the history end
policies.P3: P2's draft, length = leading j whose estimated P(1..j all accepted) > delta, capped at N; P3cond uses P(j accepted | 1..j-1) > delta instead of the product
policies.P3cost: P3 with the threshold read off the cost model: add draft j while P_j > S(j+1) - S(j), plus, for the 'today' rule, the expected replay a rejection at j would add, (P_{j-1} - P_j) * R(j-1); P3cost/<tier>/today is the variant that accounts for today's replay

code_edits.source: this repository's non-merge history up to 49f5ccb128863edf7e7226426aedfc9e5180b0e9: each modified .c/.h/.py/.md file of 0.5-64 KB; prompt = old version + one instruction line naming the path and the commit subject, output = new version

code_writing.source: Python standard library modules of 3-40 KB under /usr/lib/python3.11, outside test directories; prompt = first third (to a line boundary), output = the rest

prose.source: this repository's markdown of 2-60 KB and the evaluation half of the installed packages' markdown (npm, Ruby gems, Go); prompt = first third, output = the rest

chat.source: technical Q&A synthesized from sectioned markdown in the evaluation half of the installed packages: one user question per heading, the section as the assistant's answer, up to 10 turns; every answer is output, every question and all earlier turns are history. No real conversation transcripts were used.
